questions.q: High density polythene (HDPE) is obtained from ethene under which conditions?
options: Trace O₂ or peroxide, 1000–2000 atm, 350–570 K
Et₃Al + TiCl₄ in a hydrocarbon solvent, 6–7 atm, 333–343 K
Benzoyl peroxide, very high pressure, 570 K
questions.explain: HDPE needs the Ziegler–Natta catalyst (triethylaluminium + TiCl₄) at low pressure; the high-pressure trace-O₂ route gives branched LDPE.

questions.q: Which addition polymer is used as a substitute for wool?
questions.explain: Polyacrylonitrile (Orlon, Acrilan), made from CH₂=CH–CN with a peroxide initiator, gives fibres used in place of wool.

options: HDPE is formed by an anionic polymerisation mechanism
LDPE is branched because a growing radical abstracts an H atom from another chain
PMMA is used for intraocular lenses
Chlorinated PVC is used for hot-water pipes
questions.explain: HDPE forms by coordination polymerisation: ethene coordinates to titanium and inserts into the Ti–C bond. It is not an anionic process.

questions.q: The repeating unit –CH₂–C(CH₃)(COOCH₃)– belongs to a polymer whose monomer is
questions.explain: Putting the double bond back between the two main-chain carbons gives methyl methacrylate, the monomer of PMMA (Perspex, Plexiglas).
